notes:
Verdict: I agree with all 15 rehomes to 30929531 and record HIGH on each. Ruling 3's conclusion holds, but one of its supporting facts does not discriminate, and the profile evidence points to NENC.

1. Where the reviewer overstates. "NENC listed separately (reviewBody) in 14 of 15" comes from the PSR form's review-body slot, and the same account fills that slot beside NENC-named buyers too:
   - 013052-2024 (46937325, 2024-04-22, the day before the run starts): buyer named NENC, reviewOrg GB-FTS-107692;
   - 013745-2024 (46937905, 2024-04-29, NENC-named, published between two of the 15): reviewOrg GB-FTS-109824;
   - 038756-2024: reviewBody GB-FTS-107692.

   Apart from its name, the buyer party in the 15 matches the NENC-named 13T buyers exactly: code 13T, details.url northeastnorthcumbria.nhs.uk, Stella House NE15 8NY, necsu.psrprocurement mailbox. All 15 say "The relevant authority intends to award", and their decision makers are NENC ICB officers. So the precise reading is that NECS, the agent, entered its own exact legal name as the contracting party for NENC's PSR awards. It is not NECS acting as a separate party alongside NENC.

2. Why HIGH still holds:
   - "NORTH OF ENGLAND COMMISSIONING SUPPORT" (name and identifier.legalName) is another body's exact legal name, not an NENC misspelling. Under §1.4's test that makes it a rehome, not a hold.
   - The naming was persistent, not a one-off typo. The July 2024 follow-up (tenderUpdate) notices of 13 of these 15 procurements name the same party in the same uppercase form, now under NENC's ICB code GB-NHS-QHM. The 14 follow-up mentions are 46895004, 46895225, 46895228, 46895248, 46895261, 46895377, 46895693, 46895696, 46896093, 46896410, 46896414, 47163849, 47164020 and 47164026.
   - Those 14 already sit on NECS's provisional row 3257070, which 513's reviewed QHM verdict classed DIFFERENT (NECS 0AR). Rehoming keeps both notices of each procurement on NECS.
   - Lifecycle (013689) and AQP Podiatry (013850) have no follow-up in that set. Qwell (013310) has no NENC party at all.

3. Target and live state:
   - Target: 30929531 answered HTTP 200 with no redirect: provisional=false, PPON PJGL8154MTZX, merged GBNHS0AR, 55 mentions. ODS 0AR is "NHS NORTH OF ENGLAND COMMISSIONING SUPPORT UNIT" (RO213, Active). The other NECS-named rows are 3257070 (provisional, 253 mentions), 10286686 (country US, provisional) and 31600907 (13T itself), so 30929531 is the right row.
   - Mentions: a live primary-key seek on organization_mentions shows all 15 tuples (notice_id, 'ORG-GB-NHS-13T') still on organization_id 31600907, named "NORTH OF ENGLAND COMMISSIONING SUPPORT", raw GB-NHS-13T.
   - Follow-up (not in scope here): 3257070 should be consolidated into 30929531. Until then, each procurement's award and follow-up notices sit on two NECS rows.

The parties block still shows the old name 'NHS England - North East & Yorkshire', and so does our stored parse (/v1/notices/46991199/content: BT-500 has that name, and nothing of the correction was ingested). Everything else points to NENC acting through NECS: the description says 'NECS is working for and on behalf of North East and North Cumbria ICB (The Contracting Authority)' and 'The ICB is inviting any provider'; the code is GB-NHS-13T, NENC's own sub-ICB child code; the contact is necsu.neprocurement@nhs.net; the address is NECS's (Waterfront 4 Goldcrest Way, NE15 8NY); the buyer profile is in-tendhost.co.uk/nhsnecsu. It would be the right row for NHS England NEY, but the notice withdraws that name, so (b) is wrong on the evidence, not just MEDIUM: it would move an NENC tender onto NHS England. 31556600 returns 200 and is live (PPON PMYZ6944BYLH, GBNHSQHM merged, 2,395 mentions, not provisional).
